papers.title: Pairing AIS with RF: Analysis of a Markovian Approach for Maritime Data Fusion
papers.summary: Monitoring maritime activities is important for safety and security, particularly for detecting illegal activities, but remains challenging due to the size and complexity of the maritime domain. The Automatic Identification System (AIS) is commonly used for this purpose, despite its known vulnerabilities. In contrast, space-based radio frequency (RF) observations provide an independent source of vessel activity but lack ship identification and therefore cannot identify vessels on their own. Following the CRISP-DM process, this study applies a Pair Hidden Markov Model (PHMM) to align individual RF detections with AIS trajectories, using temporal and spatial information while modeling noise and timing discrepancies. We evaluate it on NOAA AIS data with synthetic RF detections against nearest-neighbor baselines and analyze its errors with bias tests on trajectory length, sampling density, stationarity and AIS--RF distance. The length-corrected Forward score reaches a top-1 precision of $0.7776$ on the validation split of multi-candidate detections, where errors are possible, and an AUC of $0.637$ for detecting dark vessels among the detections that pass the prefilter. With a single RF detection, the score mostly reflects the AIS trajectory itself, and its errors favor longer and more stationary trajectories. A log-odds score, which compares the full model with a null model without match transitions, raises precision to $0.8580$ and AUC to $0.852$. Its length-corrected variant no longer shows a significant bias towards stationary trajectories and short inter-message distances, but still favors candidates farther from the RF detection. A time-weighted nearest-neighbor baseline without fitting remains ahead (precision $0.9013$, AUC $0.904$), so this single-detection, hand-designed PHMM formulation approaches but does not beat it.
papers.comment: 10 pages, 5 figures, accepted at the 13th IEEE Special Session Privacy and Security of Big Data of IEEE BigData 2026

papers.title: FETTUCCINE: Fast and efficient brain-to-text decoding on mobile devices
papers.summary: Recent advances in speech neuroprostheses have enabled new communication avenues for people who have lost the ability to speak due to neurological illness or injury. These systems can decode neural activity during attempted speech into text by relying on language priors to achieve high decoding accuracy. This performance currently comes at the cost of using a compute-intensive language modeling stack, presenting a major bottleneck for real-world use. Further, current language models incur highly variable and disruptive inference latencies, limiting communication throughput and preventing users from reliably participating in natural conversation. We introduce FETTUCCINE, an end-to-end brain-to-text framework that leverages the speed and portability of automatic speech recognition (ASR) models to address the aforementioned practical challenges, while achieving usable (<10%) word error rates (WER), efficient adaptation to neural non-stationarities, and reliable performance on mobile devices. When evaluated using publicly available data from an intracortical speech neuroprosthesis user, FETTUCCINE outperforms previous end-to-end methods, achieving as low as 4.39% WER. Most notably, our models successfully run on a commercially-available mobile device with throughput reaching up to 370x real-time, providing the first demonstration of brain-to-text decoding on a mobile device. We also show that our models can be successfully finetuned to extend usable performance to future days. Beyond performance, our approach enables localization of the neural features most relevant for decoding via gradient-based saliency maps, which we show align with well-established physiological priors across different ASR model families. Taken together, our results show that FETTUCCINE overcomes core infrastructural and computational barriers, yielding a new class of portable brain-to-text communication.

papers.title: Training Reasoning Models in Simulation to Natively Use Real Robots
papers.summary: Robot-use agents (RUAs) have emerged as a promising approach to general-purpose robot control. However, strong performance has so far been achieved only by frontier proprietary models such as GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.2, whereas open-weight models remain substantially less capable. We show that an open-weight 27B reasoning model can be trained to use real robots natively through reinforcement learning, entirely in simulation and without demonstrations. Like a computer-use agent (CUA), the model observes the environment, reasons in a chain of thought, and generates the next end-effector pose, without any harness. We build a Post-training Engine for Agentic Robotics (PEAR) and use it to train the model on simulated robot tasks at scale with robot-use reinforcement learning (RURL), mirroring how frontier models acquire computer use. We find that the skills acquired in simulation generalize well beyond the training tasks: they transfer to an unseen robot, to the real world, and to novel instructions. After training on LIBERO and RoboDojo in simulation, the model succeeds in 60% of our trials on a real dual-arm robot, whereas the base model succeeds in none. On LIBERO, training raises the success rate from 1.6% to 74.4%, approaching GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol at maximum reasoning effort. Compared with $π_{0.5}$, a vision-language-action model fine-tuned on demonstrations, our model is substantially more robust to changes in the task itself. On LIBERO-Pro, $π_{0.5}$ succeeds in only 0.75% of episodes when assigned a new task in a familiar scene whereas our model succeeds in 57.4%. Finally, the model retains its general capabilities, with no measurable degradation on nine reasoning, coding and vision benchmarks. These results highlight robot-use reinforcement learning as a promising component of foundation-model post-training.

papers.title: On the pure part of the cohomology of character varieties
papers.summary: We prove the purity conjecture of Hausel and Rodriguez-Villegas relating the graded dimension of the pure part of the cohomology of the twisted character variety $M^B(r,d)$ of $GL(r)$ of genus $g$ with the cohomology of a suitable quiver variety associated to the quiver $S_g$ with one vertex and $g$ loops. In particular, this provides an explicit formula for the pure part of the mixed Hodge polynomial of $M^B(r,d)$ in terms of the Kac polynomial $A_{S_g,r}(q)$. Our approach is based on the $P=W$ theorem to transfer the purity conjecture into a statement about the perverse filtration on the cohomology of th stack of Higgs bundles on a genus $g$ curve. We use the theory of BPS Lie algebras, their $χ$-independence property (proven by Kinjo-Koseki), the recent proof of the stack version of $P=C$ due to Picovschi and Davison's analytic neighborhood theorem to reduce the conjecture to a comparison problem between (the 'pure' part) of the BPS Lie algebra asociated to the stack of Higgs bundles on a genus $g$ curve and the BPS Lie algebra of the stack of representations of the preprojective algebra of the quiver $S_g$. This last step is taken care of by a quiver analog of Markman's tautological generation theorem for the BPS Lie algebra of arbitrary quivers (this last result is also proven by Davison and Hennecart).

papers.title: BAL: Bidirectional Autoregression in Latent Space for Learning Human Movement Representations
papers.summary: Learning semantically meaningful human movement representations from 3D pose sequences is essential for human behavior modeling. Existing self-supervised methods derive supervision from artificial assumptions, e.g., invariance to augmentation within a certain range or recoverability of masked regions at a certain temporal scale, introducing heuristic hyperparameters that make the learned semantics sensitive to their settings. We propose BAL, a self-supervised framework that instead exploits supervision intrinsic to human movement: the natural ordering structure of everyday behavior. BAL autoregressively predicts in a semantically abstract latent space, analogous to how humans anticipate others' actions rather than their precise joint configurations. Bidirectional autoregressive prediction, both forward and backward in time, fully leverages these ordering constraints while enabling representation extraction using both past and future context at inference. To suppress representation collapse, BAL decomposes each prediction target into a global component capturing sequence-level semantics and a local component capturing context-independent movement. We prove that the local targets retain nontrivial angular diversity unless the representations are completely collapsed, preserving a meaningful training signal. Experiments on large-scale datasets demonstrate that BAL's representations are highly effective for motion captioning, forecasting, and interpolation, outperforming baselines on most evaluation metrics.
papers.comment: Accepted to NeurIPS 2026. Project page: https://github.com/kyotovision-public/bal

papers.title: Reconstruction of Dynamical Dark Energy and Gravity from latest cosmological data
papers.summary: Recent cosmological observations have renewed interest in non-standard late-time evolution. We investigate whether departures from the standard expansion history are accompanied by modifications of gravitational dynamics through a joint, non-parametric reconstruction of the effective dark energy density, $Ω_{\rm X}(a)$, and the gravitational response functions $μ(a)$ and $Σ(a)$. Combining CMB, DESI DR2 BAO, Pantheon+, and large scale structure observations, including DES Year 3 $6\times2$pt data, we perform reconstructions with and without a theory motivated correlation prior derived from stable Horndeski models. We find a persistent maximum in $Ω_{\rm X}$ at $z\simeq0.5$--$0.7$, corresponding to a crossing of the effective phantom divide. This feature is already present in the CMB+BAO combination and remains robust when modifications to clustering and lensing are allowed. The reconstructed gravitational response exhibits suggestive enhancements in $μ$ and $Σ$ over approximately the same redshift range, although these departures are less significant. Including LSS information instead favours a reduced lensing response, $Σ<1$, while leaving the background feature largely unchanged. An interpretation within Generalized Brans-Dicke theories illustrates how modifications to the effective gravitational coupling and a scalar-mediated fifth force may contribute to these trends. Our results indicate that current departures from $Λ$CDM are most significant in the expansion history, while leaving open the possibility of correlated modifications to gravitational dynamics that future Stage IV surveys can test.

papers.title: Does Dark Energy Evolve $\textit{and}$ Cluster?
papers.summary: Recent cosmological observations have renewed interest in dynamical dark energy, and naturally raise the question of whether departures from the standard expansion history are accompanied by modifications of gravitational dynamics. We address this question through a joint, non-parametric reconstruction of the effective dark-energy contribution to the expansion and the gravitational responses governing clustering and lensing, complemented by a combined covariance-mode analysis, without imposing model-specific relations between the sectors. Combining CMB, DESI DR2 BAO, and Pantheon+ supernova observations, and subsequently adding large scale structure observations including DES Year 3 $6\times2$pt data and other surveys, we recover a broad maximum in the effective dark-energy density near $z\simeq0.6$--$0.7$. The gravitational responses exhibit suggestive low-redshift enhancements over their GR values, approximately coincident with the background feature. Adding large scale structure information preserves the background feature but favours a mildly reduced lensing response. The combined covariance-mode analysis identifies the combinations of background and gravitational responses most tightly constrained by current observations and quantifies their departures from $Λ$CDM. The leading modes are decisively background dominated, while the gravitational sector remains less precisely constrained. Thus, present data cannot yet determine whether the suggestive low-redshift features in the two sectors share a common physical origin, a question that ongoing Stage-IV surveys will be able to address

papers.title: From pure spinor modules to superspace superfields
papers.summary: We relate the pure spinor formalism to the superspace description of constrained superfields and gauge multiplets, mainly for abelian two-dimensional N=(2,2) supersymmetry, with three- and four-dimensional N=1 examples for comparison. For each multiplet we give an explicit module over the supertranslation Chevalley-Eilenberg algebra and match its reconstruction with the known superfields. First-order constraints come from modules supported on linear subspaces of the nilpotence variety, and higher-order ones, such as the complex-linear constraint, from Yoneda products of their Ext classes. Requiring a connection to act on given matter and its conjugate restricts its curvature, which yields the ordinary, twisted and semichiral vector multiplets with their field strengths. The module of each vector multiplet is the fiber product over the origin of the coordinate rings of the matter supports: its potentials are differences of partial potentials, and its gauge parameters are the matter superfields. For the large vector multiplet this fiber product is not a quotient of the pure spinor ring; its field strengths are four odd semichiral superfields, and partial regluing gives its constrained versions.

papers.title: Towards invertibility of derived categories of sheaf-theoretic line operators
papers.summary: We investigate when the braided monoidal $\infty$-categories of sheaf-theoretic line operators of $3$-dimensional topological quantum field theories are invertible in the higher Morita category, so that they determine invertible $4$-dimensional anomaly theories. We consider a zoo of different examples which are inherently derived. First, enhancing Ben-Zvi--Francis--Nadler, we show that a symmetric monoidal category of quasi-coherent sheaves $\mathrm{QC}(X)$ is invertible only if $X$ is a point, and convolution categories on loop stacks are Morita trivial whenever the stack satisfies descent along its diagonal, e.g. for classifying stacks. Secondly, we provide an example showing that, unlike for finite braided tensor categories, non-degeneracy does not imply invertibility in the derived setting: For an odd vector space $V[1]$, the $2$-shifted $\mathcal{D}$-modules $\mathrm{DMod}^2(V[1])$ are $3$-dualizable and non-degenerate but neither factorizable nor cofactorizable. This category is closely related to the line operators of linear Rozansky--Witten theory. Finally, we define an anomaly of a group action on an invertible braided monoidal $\infty$-category as a Witt class over $\mathrm{Rep}(G)$, and show that the category of representations of the quantum group of a torus at a root of unity is invertible relative to its quantum Frobenius.

papers.title: Sharp nonuniqueness for the Vlasov--Navier--Stokes system
papers.summary: We consider the Vlasov--Navier--Stokes system on $\mathbb T^d\times\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge2$. For smooth data and every $p<2$, $q<\infty$, we construct infinitely many weak solutions with velocity in $L^p_tL^\infty\cap L^1_tW^{1,q}$ and bounded, renormalized distribution function; infinitely many of them violate the energy inequality. For smooth velocity data, weak solutions with velocity in $L^2_tL^\infty$ are unique, so the result is sharp at the endpoint of the Ladyzhenskaya--Prodi--Serrin scale. The fluid carries the nonuniqueness, through the convex integration scheme of Cheskidov and Luo, and the kinetic equation is solved exactly. The main new difficulty is the memory of the particles: the kinetic state at time $t$ depends on the whole past of the velocity, so a modification on a short interval changes the system at all later times. We overcome it by a causal gluing, carried out from left to right in time, which re-solves the system on every interval of regularity. This yields wild solutions that are strong outside a closed set of times of arbitrarily small Hausdorff dimension. A causal mollification extends the construction to rough data, including every finite-energy velocity datum in dimensions two and three; in two dimensions the energy class is thus exactly the borderline of uniqueness. Finally, in three dimensions we construct Leray solutions satisfying the strong energy inequality and show that they are strong outside a closed set of times of vanishing $\mathcal H^{1/2}$ measure.

papers.title: WeightBench: Evaluating Language Models as Weight-Space Programmers
papers.summary: Recent work shows that large language models (LLMs) can operate directly on the parameters of other neural networks. They can read what a network was trained to do, fix a network that fails, and write working networks from scratch, all without gradient descent. This capability has been termed Weight-Space Programming (WSP). Exploring this new paradigm systematically requires a robust benchmark. We introduce WEIGHTBENCH, a benchmark that evaluates LLMs of increasing capability on 42 WSP tasks across five tracks: reading, fixing and writing weights, recognizing edits that are impossible, and data-free compression. The networks whose weights the LLMs read and edit range from 2K-parameter control policies to 7B-parameter language models. Experimental benchmark results show that frontier agents can already read small networks and write working control policies without ever running them, but cannot yet patch language models, compress them without data, or tell an impossible edit from a hard one. On all 42 tasks, Claude Opus 5.5 reaches a macro score of 0.535 (Sonnet 5.5 0.466, Haiku 5.5 0.402, DeepSeek v4-flash 0.215); on the 38 tasks it was run on, GPT-6.1-sol reaches 0.568 against Opus's 0.546. Code, the task registry, our OS-level sandbox harness, and the live leaderboard are publicly available at https://github.com/Aayush-Marasini/WeightBench.
papers.comment: 9 pages, 1 figure, 1 table. Code and leaderboard available at https://github.com/Aayush-Marasini/WeightBench

papers.title: Real-time simulation of scattering in $φ^4$ theory: localized excitation, scalable wave packet preparation, and peak-generating artifacts
papers.summary: Probing real-time dynamics is essential for understanding non-perturbative scattering and interactions in quantum field theory. A common challenge in real-time simulation is preparing accurate asymptotic incoming states. Through efficiently solvable eigenvalue problems, we jointly optimize a superposition of single particle momentum eigenstates and a single site interpolating operator to maximize preparation fidelity from the interacting vacuum. This leads to a localized excitation in the interacting theory analogous to a position eigenstate. Weighted sums of the resulting interpolating operator over lattice sites prepare wave packets of arbitrary spatial extent. To ensure that this construction produces the correct continuum limit, relative phases among single particle momentum eigenstates in this superposition are calibrated using a relation derived from Lorentz symmetry. Analyzing single particle wave packet propagation through the position space profile reveals oscillatory Airy distortions, which originate from interference between saddle point contributions at different momenta that share the same lattice group velocity. These oscillations systematically weaken when approaching the continuum limit, and reliable regimes are identified as a function of simulation time and wave packet momentum profile. Two-particle scattering simulations in interacting scalar field theory are also implemented, revealing artificial inelasticity arising from coarse local field digitization or deviation from the Nyquist-Shannon sampling point. With these artifacts under control, present simulations provide emerging evidence for physical inelastic processes in $φ^4$ theory. The constructions introduced in this work may provide new understanding of state preparation for the quantum simulation of scattering.

papers.title: Restoring Diversity in Distilled Image and Video Generators by Probing Activations
papers.summary: Distilling diffusion models into few-step student models substantially reduces sampling latency, but induces severe diversity collapse: samples generated from different random seeds show minimal variation. In this work, we investigate the root cause of this failure by probing the internal representations of student models relative to their teachers. We find that distilled students maintain total activation variance comparable to their teachers, but concentrate it into substantially fewer directions. This directional collapse is localized to an identifiable intermediate block at the initial denoising step. Consequently, diversity collapse stems from a misallocation of activation variance rather than an inherent loss of generative capacity. Guided by this finding, we propose ReDiverse to reinstate the missing variance directions. At training time, ReDiverse-FT fine-tunes a lightweight adapter that regresses student activations onto the teacher's, reviving the teacher's feature variance characteristic. At inference time, ReDiverse-TF introduces a training-free mechanism that steers activations along precomputed teacher principal directions. Across image and video distillation benchmarks, ReDiverse consistently restores sample diversity while preserving generation quality, further supported by the user study.

papers.title: JVT: Just Video Transformer makes pixel-space video diffusion simple
papers.summary: Direct diffusion modeling of high-dimensional raw video data is challenging, and existing pixel-space methods often rely on specialized architectures. We introduce JVT (Just Video Transformer), a simple large-patch DiT-style Transformer for pixel-space video diffusion, without a pretrained autoencoder, auxiliary detailers, cascaded stages, or U-Net-style skip connections. We systematically examine video patch embeddings, register tokens, and adaptive layer normalization to identify design choices that balance generation quality and computational efficiency. The resulting JVT design achieves generation quality competitive with latent diffusion baselines in both class-conditioned and unconditional settings. The pixel-space formulation of JVT also naturally supports joint generation of pixel-aligned modalities. We demonstrate this capability through camera-conditioned RGB-disparity generation, which improves camera following relative to RGB-only baselines and yields explicit scene geometry without an additional reconstruction model at inference. These results highlight the potential of simple DiT-style Transformers for pixel-space video diffusion, and we hope our findings offer useful insights and practical guidance for future research.

papers.title: Limitations of nonreversible lifts for subgeometric diffusions
papers.summary: We study the effect of lifting on continuous-time Markov processes with potentially subgeometric convergence rates. Using a series of weak Poincaré-type inequalities, we derive a bound on the maximum acceleration that can be obtained through lifting. We present several examples to explore the sharpness of our derived bound, where the resulting bound has the same square-root order as in the spectral gap setting. Our results provide a framework for understanding the potential and limitations of non-reversible lifting beyond geometric convergence.

papers.title: Polynomial-Time Solvability of the Multi-Dimensional Slope Change Problem
papers.summary: Slope change detection seeks to identify changes in the trends of time-ordered signals. We study the problem of fitting a multidimensional time series by continuous piecewise-linear functions with a shared continuous breakpoint and unrestricted slopes. We consider both the dense setting, in which every dimension may change slope, and the sparse setting, in which at most $k$ dimensions may change slope. Although the resulting optimization problems are nonconvex mixed integer nonlinear programs and may have irrational optimal solutions even for rational data, we prove that all six variants, corresponding to the $\ell_1$, $\ell_2$, and $\ell_\infty$ losses in both settings, are exactly solvable in polynomial time. For least-squares loss, we obtain efficient algorithms requiring $O(JT)$ operations in the dense setting and $O(J^2T\log J)$ operations in the sparse setting, where $T$ is the number of time points and $J$ is the number of dimensions. We implement these least-squares algorithms and evaluate them on simulated data and three real-world time series, namely, surface temperatures (ERA5), hand-tracking data from a mixed-reality headset (HoloAssist), and turbofan engine sensor data (NASA C-MAPSS). The dense algorithm solves instances with up to $J=10^5$ and $T=100$, that is, $10^7$ observations, in less than $0.1$ seconds on a laptop, while the sparse algorithm solves instances with about $10^3$ dimensions and up to $T=240$ in under a second. Compared with a mixed-integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) formulation solved by Gurobi, our algorithms are several orders of magnitude faster (approximately $8.9 \times 10^3$ to $3.4 \times 10^6$ times) on instances where Gurobi terminates within its default optimality tolerance of $0.01\%$ optimality gap. On larger instances, Gurobi frequently reaches a 10,000-second time limit with substantial optimality gaps.

papers.title: Modeling the Frictional Contact of Continuum Robots with Environments through Linear Complementarity Problem
papers.summary: Accurate friction modeling in continuum robots is essential for precise motion control and path planning. However, current approaches make predictions only for the mechanism's internal friction that is limited by the boundary forces of the Coulomb friction cone, which fail to characterize the static friction and motion hysteresis. In this paper, we propose a novel friction model based on complementarity constraints under the Coulomb friction assumption. This model predicts various friction effects caused by environmental interactions, including both static and sliding frictions and hysteresis behavior, as well as the corresponding robot deformation induced by these interactions, which are crucial for the practical motion planning and control of continuum robots. Additionally, real-time implementation of this model can be achieved, meeting the demand for computational efficiency in robotic applications. Experimental validations demonstrated that this model is able to reduce the maximum tip position error from 45.4 mm in the frictionless model to 5.85 mm in our friction-included model with a 287.9 mm-long tendon-driven continuum robot.
papers.comment: Accepted for publication in International Journal of Robotics Research (IJRR). 21 pages, 18 figures

papers.title: From smoothed analysis to backward error: The power of adaptive perturbations
papers.summary: Smoothed analysis has become a central tool in theoretical computer science, often allowing for significant improvements to worst-case running times if we settle for a solution to a small random perturbation of the problem instance. This is closely related to the classical concept of backward error in numerical analysis, which allows an algorithm to return a solution to an arbitrary perturbation of the problem. Despite the qualitative similarity of these concepts, we show that they can exhibit large quantitative differences. Notably, we prove that, while a linear system with any $n \times n$ matrix $A$ can be solved to backward error $ε$ using $O(\log(n) / ε)$ matrix-vector products with $A$, any algorithm that solves a random $ε$-sized perturbation of $A$ requires $Ω(n)$ matrix-vector products. This means that a useful perturbation for solving a linear system in backward error must be adaptive to the input. Interestingly, however, randomness is still essential: we show that any deterministic method that attains small backward error for all linear systems provably requires $Ω(n)$ matrix-vector products, resulting in the first separation between randomized and deterministic algorithms in a natural computational model for solving linear systems. Finally, we show that matrix structure can significantly affect backward error complexity. For example, we show a deterministic $O(1/ε)$ matrix-vector product algorithm for symmetric linear systems.

papers.title: Imitation Bootstrapped Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: Demonstrations are an effective way to accelerate single-agent reinforcement learning (RL), but extending this idea to multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) is non-trivial as it is difficult and often impossible for a single person to teleoperate multiple agents simultaneously. Round-Robin Behavior Cloning (R2BC) addresses this by letting a single demonstrator control one agent at a time while the others execute their current policies. However, the resulting imitation policies are limited by the quality of the demonstrations. We propose Imitation Bootstrapped Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (IBMARL), a framework that extends Imitation Bootstrapped Reinforcement Learning (IBRL) to cooperative teams and uses R2BC to train the imitation policies. At each time step, every agent receives one action proposal from its imitation policy and one from its RL policy, and an ensemble of centralized critics selects among the per-agent combinations of the two. A gated imitation penalty, a soft Q-filtered behavior cloning loss, regularizes each RL policy toward its imitation policy only where the critics value the imitation action more, so that after training each agent executes its RL policy alone, without the centralized critics. On four cooperative multi-agent RL benchmarks, IBMARL surpasses its imitation policies $2.6$-$4.2\times$ faster than demonstration-based baselines on two tasks, is the only method to surpass it on the other two, and exceeds the demonstrator itself on two of the four. With real human demonstrations IBMARL still surpasses imitation learning alone, and does so more than twice as fast as the best baseline.
papers.comment: 9 pages, 5 figures. Code, videos and results: https://zhanghutony.github.io/ibmarl/. A preliminary version appeared at the PhysCollaBot Workshop at IROS 2026

papers.title: Elliptic Sampling: Optimal Interpolant Schedules for Gaussians and Beyond
papers.summary: Generative modeling based on stochastic interpolants requires specifying two key choices: an interpolant schedule bridging the initial and target distributions, and an efficient discretization of the resulting probability-flow ODE. In this work, we introduce a new framework for joint schedule/discretization design based on the analyticity properties of the (complexified) ODE trajectories, which in turn ensure good numerical behavior. Our formulation can be solved exactly via conformal mapping, yielding a natural family of variance-preserving elliptic schedules, parametrized by Jacobi elliptic functions. Pairing an elliptic schedule with a tailored discretization, we obtain Zoloflow, a new sampling algorithm closely connected to Zolotarev's optimal rational function approximants. Crucially, both the elliptic schedule and Zoloflow explicitly incorporate the condition number $κ$ of the target distribution and reduce to the classical trig schedule in the limit $κ\rightarrow 1$. For Gaussian targets, Zoloflow achieves minimax optimality among all oblivious score-span algorithms, attaining total-variation error $\varepsilon$ using $Θ(\logκ\,\log(\sqrt d/\varepsilon))$ (exact) score queries. For the log-concave case, the elliptic schedule allows sampling with at most $\varepsilon$ 2-Wasserstein-error by requiring merely $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{d} \, \mathrm{polylog}(κ, 1/\varepsilon))$ score evaluations. Complementing these theoretical results, we empirically evaluate the elliptic schedule on general (non-log-concave) target distributions, including detailed comparisons with alternative schedule proposals on both synthetic benchmarks and existing image generation datasets.

papers.title: Internal diameter bounds for DLA on random planar maps under invariance principles
papers.summary: We establish sublinear bounds for the internal diameter of External Diffusion Limited Aggregation (DLA) clusters on random planar maps. We develop two conditional DLA growth results for deterministic planar maps: the weaker condition yielding sublinear growth for DLA, and the stronger yielding polynomially sublinear growth for DLA. We then verify the strong assumption a.s. for the $γ$-mated CRT maps, and the weak condition a.s. for ergodic scale-free random environments, establishing the corresponding a.s bounds.

papers.title: Geometric Quantization of the Giant Graviton Master Moduli Space
papers.summary: We describe a remarkable reorganization of the space of gauge invariant operators of free or twisted $U(N)$ gauge theories as combinations of single-trace and determinant operators modulo certain "open loop equations". The reorganization has a transparent holographic interpretation, describing how states at finite $N$ can be reproduced by imposing certain $N$-independent gauge constraints on the combination of the closed strings Fock space and a geometric quantization of the moduli space of Giant Graviton D-branes, with quantization parameter $N^{-1}$. The moduli space of Giant Graviton D-branes is reproduced from tachyon condensation of auxiliary D-brane/anti-D-brane pairs which are "Koszul dual" to the D-brane system which supports the original gauge theory. We describe how to impose the open loop equations via certain BRST complexes and conjecture that their homology recovers the finite $N$ BPS Hilbert space in the limit of large auxiliary rank. The BRST construction conjecturally categorifies Murthy's Giant Graviton Expansion of indices counting $U(N)$-invariant BPS operators.

papers.title: Why Finite Intelligence Works in an Infinite World: A Mathematical Theory
papers.summary: An information system often has to learn before it knows what it will be asked. A finite representation can succeed without recording an infinite environment in full when those asks share collective structure, rather than demand unrelated facts scattered arbitrarily across it. We formalize this phenomenon through future-task information, the minimum retained information needed to preserve decision value relative to the available evidence. A joint decision-regret state records posterior comparisons among actions for every permitted task. Under compactness assumptions, every retained representation admits a calibrated replacement based on this state, preserving all task regrets without increasing information; the resulting information-regret curve equals an operational coding rate. Two exact boundaries govern finite preservation: weak-star closure for a fixed action count, and the singular mass of the source-evidence law when all finite action menus are admitted. Collective structure determines information requirements beyond individual-question difficulty. Families with identical source laws, pairwise task metrics, and individual-task rates can have different high-resolution exponents. Covariance-identical coordinate and parity families have different exact rate-distortion curves, with optimal parity retention characterized by a sharp Fourier-entropy inequality. For balanced nested task families, refinement sizes and weighted reach determine the rate within an additive constant, attained by prefix coding under explicit decay conditions. Nonlinear learning and computational separations distinguish preservation from efficient discovery and use. The proposed mathematical theory identifies which shared decision requirements allow finite information to remain useful for infinitely many possible purposes.

papers.title: Valid Inequalities for Bilevel 0-1 Shortest-Path Problems
papers.summary: We characterize valid inequalities for bilevel programs in which the leader makes binary decisions, and the follower solves a shortest-path problem. We exploit a dualize-and-combine reformulation and show that even with ideal formulations for the leader and the follower primal solution sets, fractional solutions may still appear in the continuous relaxation. From that reformulation, we identify that the interaction between the leader variables and the follower dual variables, which we capture through a leader-potential set, is the key structure to be convexified to guarantee that a continuous relaxation recovers the optimal value of the original problem, closing the objective gap. Furthermore, we characterize the valid inequalities for the leader-potential set through network flows, and identify a family of inequalities we name root cuts that suffice to recover the optimal value. Complementary to the structural results, we prove that the cut generation problem is NP-hard even with partially fixed coefficients and a network with two nodes and two parallel arcs. Motivated by the complexity result, we propose a constructive method to fix coefficients in the valid inequalities while preserving separation guarantees, by exploiting the network structure.

papers.title: On Zhao's conjectural basis for finite multiple zeta values
papers.summary: We prove a conjecture by J. Zhao which states that every finite multiple zeta value associated with a nonempty index is a $\mathbb{Q}$-linear combination of $ζ^{}_{\mathcal{A}}(k_1,\dots, k_r, 2, 1)$, where $k_i\in \{2, 3\}$. Our proof proceeds by constructing a basis for the space of formal multiple zeta values defined by the confluence relations. This approach also reduces the Kaneko--Zagier conjecture (apart from compatibility with the depth filtration) to linear independence conjectures for ordinary and finite multiple zeta values, without using motivic theory.

papers.title: A Surrogate Boundary Condition for Improved Accuracy and Performance of Local Modeling in Radiation Transport Simulations
papers.summary: Monte Carlo neutronics analysis of tokamak designs is computationally expensive due to the complex CAD geometries required to accurately model them. Design iteration of port plugs using global transport in the full model is impractical because of the computational cost. To circumvent this, local modeling methods are used. In the local modeling method, a boundary condition is assumed on the port plug, such that particles that leave the port plug do not require transport in the surrounding global model. For this purpose, vacuum and reflective boundaries are assumed, both of which provide poor approximation of the true transport physics in the global model. To improve on current techniques, a surrogate model is presented that provides a physics-informed boundary condition for the component. A neural network is trained to reproduce the boundary condition on the component that represents the behavior of particles returning from the surrounding geometry. Monte Carlo transport is only necessary within the component, and approximate physics from the surrounding region are retained. This approach allows the design in the component to be iterated without requiring full model transport and joining of the component mesh to the global mesh in each iteration. In this work, the surrogate model is evaluated against vacuum and reflective boundaries-- outperforming both in accuracy, with surrogate predictions of the flux in the port plug differing less than 12% from the global transport solution in any given energy bin. The surrogate boundary condition is also demonstrated to be more performant than global transport for the simplified benchmark geometry.

papers.title: Impact of Grid-Forming Inverter Placement and Penetration on Local and Aggregate Frequency
papers.summary: Modern power systems are undergoing a huge shift in generation mix, including inverter-based resources that are fundamentally changing the stability dynamics of the grid. Thus, synchronous Generators (SG) are gradually being displaced by Grid-forming inverters (GFM) that are proposed as a solution to continue supporting grid stability. However, the effect of GFM placement in the network on frequency performance and how well aggregate-frequency assessment captures placement sensitivity observed in local frequency metrics remains unclear. This paper evaluates all SG and droop-controlled GFM assignments in the IEEE 39-bus system. A reduced-order model is used for the exhaustive search with load disturbances applied separately at every eligible load bus while considering nadir and Rate of Change of Frequency (RoCoF) derived from both device rating weighted aggregate frequency and local bus frequencies. Results reveal that at fixed GFM penetration, placement produced up to 104 mHz variation in worst-case local nadir and 0.21 Hz/s in maximum local RoCoF. Aggregate-frequency assessment reduced the apparent across placements by 89\% for nadir and 88\% for RoCoF at 50\% GFM penetration. These results indicate that aggregate-frequency assessment alone may obscure favorable or adverse placement effects on local frequency performance.

papers.title: ModHarness-RL: Recasting Harnesses as Learnable and Evolving Programs for Agentic RL
papers.summary: Agentic reinforcement learning (RL) increasingly relies on a harness, the scaffold around the model that decides what it sees of its own interaction and what guidance it receives. Most existing approaches train under a hand-written harness that stays fixed throughout. However, an effective harness depends on the domain, the data and the model, and keeps changing as the model trains. We introduce ModHarness-RL, which recasts the harness as programs that are learned from data and evolve as the model trains with RL. ModHarness-RL records the interaction as structured State, a set of typed blocks, and two core components of the harness are programs over these blocks, a Compression program that assembles the accumulated history into the model's context and a Steering program that supplies guidance when behavior deviates. During RL training, candidate programs are proposed from recent trajectories, verified by execution, and replayed over past trajectories, so the harness tracks how the model's behavior shifts. We study CodeSearch in depth and further analyze ALFWorld and BIRD SQL, with models from 1.5B to 8B. The proposed Compression and Steering mechanisms improve held-out performance over the fixed-harness baseline in most settings. These results suggest that a harness for agentic RL can be learned from the task's data and evolved with the model.

papers.title: Quantum melting and Pomeranchuk effect of zero-field Wigner solids
papers.summary: Wigner solids and crystals are many-body phases of matter in which repulsive interactions between the charge carriers cause them to freeze into a solid. How Wigner solids compete or cooperate with integer and fractional quantum Hall liquids has been a long-standing open question. Here, we investigate this question for zero-field, electron and hole Wigner solids in cadmium arsenide quantum wells. In the low temperature limit, our results are consistent with a recent theoretical model [A. P. Reddy and L. Fu, Phys. Rev. B 113, L161403 (2026)] that proposes that the quantum Hall liquid can become energetically favored over the solid at low integer filling factors. Going beyond the low-temperature limit, we observe a re-entrant solid that emerges from the quantum Hall liquid. We explain this observation by considering the role of spin entropy, in close analogy with the zero-field Pomeranchuk effect, but appearing here at finite fields. The competition between quantum Hall liquids and Wigner solids is thus governed by both energy and entropy terms, giving rise to rich phase stability diagrams that result from the interplay between topology and correlations.
papers.comment: Accepted for publication in npj Quantum Materials

papers.title: Alignment by Socialization: Learning Tradeoffs Under Selection
papers.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) agents are expected to complete tasks while following rules of conduct, but these objectives can conflict. We study how evolutionary selection shapes an agent's choices between them, and whether experience can make those choices reflect human judgments and withstand subsequent pressures. In our model, copies of an agent face a common uncertain reward state, and only those taking the rewarded action reproduce. We show that long-run growth is maximized when each action is taken as often as the environment rewards it. We compare three policies. A task-only policy thrives in a sandbox rewarding completion alone but fails when conduct matters. A fixed linear policy increasingly favors task completion as its stakes rise, even where humans never reward it. A learned policy instead converges to the tradeoffs rewarded by its environment; when humans supply the rewards, we call this socialization. Accumulated experience makes socialization harder to reverse under subsequent task-only training, although violations can arise before the prevailing disposition changes, and finite memory weakens this protection. When a single violation can end a deployment, a hard prohibition can prevent it, but a mistaken prohibition can also be costly. Experiments with small neural networks illustrate how training targets and memory shape these outcomes. Our results suggest that alignment depends not only on the objectives assigned to agents, but also on the environments that shape and sustain their behavior.

papers.title: Understanding Contextual Bias in Agricultural CNNs Through Hidden-Neuron Concept Induction
papers.summary: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) can classify images using background-dominated patches that contain little or none of the target object, showing that they exploit contextual information. Previous studies detected this behavior through classification accuracy but say little about what CNN hidden layers represent. We investigate whether Concept Induction can reveal interpretable visual properties associated with hidden-neuron activations on contextual image patches. Using five agricultural datasets with high, moderate, and low contextual bias, we analyze four CNN architectures at three network depths and five patch locations. Quantitative image descriptors of each patch are encoded in a knowledge graph and used as background knowledge for Concept Induction, which derives logical expressions characterizing neuron activation. These expressions are tested on held-out images using the Mann-Whitney U test and Cliff's delta. Of 48,013 tested neuron-feature pairs, 13,164 (27.4%) were validated. Validation was most frequent at intermediate depths (mean 40.2% at mid layers versus 12.0% at deep layers), and no patch location dominated across datasets. Among the tested descriptors, edge, Gabor, and Tamura texture features had the highest validation rates. Stronger contextual bias did not correspond to higher neuron-feature validation rates: moderately biased Sugarcane had the highest rate (40.5%) and highly biased Cassava the lowest (19.2%). These results suggest that behavioral context dependence and the semantic interpretability of hidden neurons capture different aspects of CNN behavior, and that Concept Induction can complement patch-based bias detection.

papers.title: KELP v1.0: an agent-ready Lagrangian particle tracker for unstructured meshes and HEALPix grids
papers.summary: Lagrangian particle tracking follows virtual particles in the velocity fields of an ocean model to study transport pathways, connectivity and dispersion. Setting up such a study takes many technical steps, and this work is increasingly done with coding agents, programs in which a language model writes code, runs it and checks the result. We present KELP v1.0, the Kinematic Engine for Lagrangian Particles, a tracker for unstructured ocean-model meshes and HEALPix grids that is built to be operated by such agents. KELP computes two- and three-dimensional trajectories with established methods on triangular, quadrilateral and mixed meshes, with global FESOM2 and coastal FESOM-C meshes as examples, and on HEALPix, the equal-area grid on which kilometre-scale digital twins distribute their output. Documentation and short task instructions, called skills, tell an agent how to prepare releases and configurations, run calculations and process the trajectories. An agent prepared and ran all experiments of this paper with these skills, and most of the preparation was completed within hours. In a controlled evaluation, the skills raised the completeness of study files prepared by five language models from 75-93% to 88-100%. KELP reproduced the particle distributions of two other trackers on the same fields. Trajectories on HEALPix fields converged to those on the model mesh as the pixels were refined. After one year, the median distance between the two was 1.6 km at a pixel spacing of 25.5 km. HEALPix output can therefore be used for Lagrangian studies of ensemble statistics when the original mesh is not available. In a 63-year calculation with 7.92 million particles released in the Beaufort Gyre, transport from the gyre to Fram Strait took years to decades, and the run took 3 h 36 min on one 128-core node. A test tracked $10^{10}$ particles on a HEALPix mesh of 35.5 million wet surface nodes.

papers.title: WaferTetris: Efficient Freeform Mapping on Wafer-Scale Accelerators
papers.summary: Wafer-scale accelerators offer massive compute capacity through hundreds of thousands of processing elements (PEs) interconnected across a single wafer, but realizing this potential requires efficient application mapping. Their scale makes programming these systems and mapping applications onto them challenging. Existing approaches rely on template-based mappings to maintain productivity, but these templates restrict the mapping design space. In particular, they impose fixed geometric layouts over the PE grid, often leaving compute and memory resources underutilized. In this work, we present WaferTetris, a system that removes these geometric restrictions through freeform mapping. Its Tetris-like strategy flexibly packs computation across the wafer, improving PE utilization and usable memory capacity while preserving PE-task code. We develop a recurrence-based throughput model that captures branch-and-join dependencies to guide spatial parallelism, and an architecture model with per-color gates that enable existing FPGA place-and-route algorithms to enforce WSE routing constraints. We evaluate WaferTetris on Cerebras WSE-3 using LLM decoding and scientific stencil benchmarks. For LLM decoding, it achieves up to $4.42\times$ the system throughput of a template-based automatic mapping baseline on the same fabric size. Compared with the manually optimized WaferLLM, WaferTetris supports $1.8\times$ the context length for LLaMA3.1-8B (80k versus 44k), while delivering equal or higher per-user throughput at matched context lengths, up to $1.10\times$.

papers.title: Three-dimensional parton structure in QCD with CP-violation
papers.summary: The Energy-Momentum tensor encodes the mechanical properties of a system such as the internal distributions energy, momentum, forces, and particle fluxes. The QCD energy momentum tensor respects CP symmetry even when QCD is modified with a CP-violating $θ$-term. In this theory, there are 5 unique generalized form factors in the Lorentz decomposition of the total Energy Momentum tensor and 3 more which only vanish when summing over all flavors. We introduce two new lightcone GPDs whose Mellin moments give the electromagnetic and gravitational form factors. These generalize the observables for QCD-based CP violation such as the neutron electric dipole moment to three dimensional light cone structure.

papers.title: Pressure and Magnetic Field Control of Topology in Antiferromagnetic Bilayers
papers.summary: Controlling band topology in magnetic semiconductors requires strategies that couple electronic structure to experimentally accessible degrees of freedom. Here we propose a cooperative approach based on pressure and magnetic reorientation in A-type antiferromagnetic bilayers. Antiparallel layer magnetizations suppress hybridization between exchange-polarized band-edge states, limiting their response to interlayer compression. A magnetic field that aligns the layer moments removes this spin mismatch, enabling pressure-enhanced hybridization to drive a band inversion. The magnetization direction then controls the symmetries of the inverted bands and whether spin--orbit coupling produces a Chern-insulating gap or symmetry-protected nodal crossings. First-principles calculations for bilayer CrSBr illustrate this mechanism within a compressed orthorhombic structural model. Out-of-plane magnetization yields a Chern insulator with a chiral edge state, whereas in-plane magnetization supports a two-dimensional Weyl semimetal with node-connecting edge states. Continuous spin canting further demonstrates how magnetic reorientation can drive the transition and stabilize the Chern phase before full magnetic saturation. Although material-specific transition conditions depend on electronic correlations and structural stability under compression, the underlying strategy identifies interlayer hybridization as a link between magnetic order and band topology. These results provide a design principle for externally tunable topological phases in layered antiferromagnetic semiconductors.

papers.title: EventSpikeSeg: Memory-Aware Mixed-Signal Architecture for Event-Camera Spiking Segmentation
papers.summary: Event-camera segmentation requires persistent neural state despite sparse input events, making memory organization a central constraint on embedded implementation. We present EventSpikeSeg, a mixed-signal architecture combining resident capacitor memory with shared analog processing in GF180MCU 180-nm CMOS. Its 25-population spiking encoder-decoder has 143,824 synaptic weights but requires 30,976,000 membrane states at 440 x 640 resolution. The mapping specifies chronological 5-ms model updates, digital event/address services and 64-state capacitor banks. Characterization covers 22 module families and 74 operating points, distinguishing transistor simulations from digital-library estimates. Nominal results include 41.711 microwatts biased neuron-core power, 3.338-pJ positive terminal energy for a 1.4-microsecond cell read, and 0.531-mV selected-state drift over a 5-ms extracted-tile hold. Commit and coupling errors are reported separately. The software checkpoint records 27.976% mean intersection-over-union on a held-out six-class DSEC split; this is not hardware accuracy. Component layouts and simulation evidence quantify local implementation costs and expose storage replication and service scheduling as scaling constraints. A detailed SPICE-calibrated behavioral forward simulation of one full-resolution DSEC frame achieves 24.26% mean intersection-over-union, versus 26.22% for the matched PyTorch reference, using a compact 5-fF bank variant and external count/voltage calibration. Physical full-network operation, system energy and mismatch robustness remain unverified.

papers.title: Fibonacci Non-Abelian Quantum Hall States with Pair Structure - a classification of chiral 2-cluster many-body wave-functions
papers.summary: Fibonacci anyons support universal topological quantum computation. They have been proposed to emerge in fractional quantum Hall (FQH) systems, such as the filling-fraction $ν=\tfrac{2}{3}$ state described by an effective $SU(3)_2$ Chern-Simons theory, and the $ν=\tfrac{2}{5}$ state with a $3$-cluster structure (an $n$-cluster structure means that $n$-electron bound states form a Laughlin-type wave function of the form $(z^{(n)}_i-z^{(n)}_j)^m$). In this work, we systematically classify FQH wave functions $P(z_1,\ldots,z_N)$ in the $N\rightarrow\infty$ limit, through a generalized pattern of zeros (gPOZ) approach, where the wave function is determined by the leading order of zero along with the accompanying leading polynomial that develops as successive number of $z_i$'s are brought together. Within this approach, we obtain a $(ν,h,c)$-classification of wave functions with a $2$-cluster (pair) structure. Among these wave functions, those with $(h,c) = (\tfrac12,\tfrac12)$, $(\tfrac32,\tfrac{7}{10})$, $(3,\tfrac45)$ correspond to gapped FQH states with filling fraction $ν$ and edge-state chiral central charge $c+1$, while others with $c<0$ may be gapless. We find that even a $2$-cluster structure can give rise to Fibonacci statistics, for $(ν,h,c) = (\tfrac14,\tfrac32,\tfrac{7}{10})$, corresponding to the $(5,4)$ minimal model, and for $(ν,h,c) = (\tfrac17,3,\tfrac45)$, corresponding to the $(6,5)$ minimal model. We further construct an ideal $4$-body Hamiltonian whose ground state is the $(\tfrac14,\tfrac32,\tfrac{7}{10})$ state.

papers.title: The Spectral Anatomy of Complex-Time Singularities
papers.summary: The properties of the bulk spacetime in a holographic theory may be probed by the analytic structure of the boundary correlator $G(t,x)$. In this letter, we analyse the singularities of $G(t,x)$ by deriving them from Fourier space. We show that the quasinormal modes are characterised by two distinct momentum scaling regimes. The first regime is defined by a finite $k/ω^γ$ for some characteristic exponent $γ$ which is extracted from the singularity, and probes $G(t,0)$, reproducing the bouncing geodesic analysis. The second regime is defined by a finite $k/ω$, and probes the complexified bulk away from the singularity, which allows us to study the singularities of $G(t,x\neq 0)$. We extract coefficients and exponents of the singularities for general spacetime dimensions, and allow for more exotic interiors. The heavy reliance of our computation on quasinormal modes opens the doors to a similar analysis being done on spacetimes that are accessible only numerically.

papers.title: Box-conditional Hypothesis Testing for Out-of-Distribution Object Detection
papers.summary: Detecting out-of-distribution (OOD) objects is essential for ensuring the reliability and safety of object detectors in real-world deployment. We treat the decision on a detected box as a hypothesis test with the null hypothesis that the box covers an object of an in-distribution (ID) class. The null distribution changes with the size of the box and its contact with the image border, and the detector observes both. The test can therefore rank a box only against ID boxes of the same size and border contact, which gives a distribution-free bound on the false-alarm rate for each of them and uncovers the separation that one null distribution hides. The power of the test also rests on the layer it reads. Layers built only for the ID classes have no reason to keep what sets an unknown object apart, so the test reads the features before them. We propose \textbf{PLUM}, a training-free score that pools the last backbone stage inside the box and ranks its distance to the ID classes among ID boxes of the same size and border contact. On the standard benchmark, PLUM reaches the highest AUROC among the compared methods without external models, with 91.5 and 94.5 on PASCAL-VOC and 95.1 and 97.5 on BDD100K. Code: https://github.com/DDOZMI/PLUM

papers.title: Polytopal realization of double root free subword complexes
papers.summary: We give a convex geometric sufficient condition for a convex polytope to realize a spherical subword complex. Using this criterion, we first prove that each root independent spherical subword complex is polytopal, for any Coxeter group. Then we prove the polytopality of double root free subword complexes, for any Coxeter groups. To prove this, we construct a polytope in an auxiliary vector space whose image under a natural affine map is the usual brick polytope. In the complex Kac-Moody case, the polytope is integral, with vertices in the character lattice of the torus of unfolded galleries in a thick building. In finite Lie types, in double root free cases, these tori are precisely the corresponding braid varieties.

papers.title: StreamEmbed: Real-Time Indexing from Pixels for Screenshot Retrieval
papers.summary: Screen history can serve as searchable visual memory for people and agents, but unlike an offline corpus, it must be encoded and indexed as each screenshot arrives. OCR-based indexing is fast but loses visual information; visual encoding takes over two seconds. Yet screens change incrementally: most pixels repeat within and across screenshots. This raises a question: do visual encoders need to recompute their representations from scratch for every new screenshot? We present StreamEmbed, a system for incremental visual embedding that exploits this redundancy. Guided solely by pixel differences, it combines spatial token pruning, which skips blocks that repeat a neighbor, with temporal KV reuse, which reuses cached keys and values for blocks unchanged across screenshots. A small learned adapter compensates for pruning and reuse to preserve fidelity to full-screenshot embeddings. On ScreenMemEval, our benchmark of 10,426 questions over 184 hours of screen histories from two humans and a computer-use agent, StreamEmbed sets a new accuracy-latency Pareto frontier on an M2 Pro GPU: it encodes up to 3.7x faster than full-screenshot encoding without sacrificing accuracy and improves accuracy over OCR-based indexing by up to 6.3 Recall@10 points at matched latency. A memory-efficient vector index stores a simulated year of screenshots in 0.13 GB of RAM. Together, these results make real-time indexing of screen history in its native visual form practical, laying a foundation for fully local visual assistants.

papers.title: Parity conservation of the isotropic galaxy 4PCF in redshift space
papers.summary: Recent observational investigation of cosmological Parity Violation (PV) through the galaxy Four-point Correlation Function (4PCF) has motivated a careful theoretical examination of potential systematic contributions. In this work, we demonstrate that parity-odd contributions to the isotropic 4PCF estimator induced by Redshift Space Distortion (RSD), up to the leading order $\mathcal{H}/k$ of general relativistic corrections, vanish upon averaging over all the Line-of-Sight (LOS). We analyse the perturbative relativistic galaxy number density, combining the biased tracer expansion and the dark matter gravitational dynamics within the framework of Standard Eulerian Perturbation Theory (EPT) to third order in the density perturbation. Building on prior studies of the parity-odd mode of the trispectrum (the Fourier-space counterpart of the 4PCF), we extend existing results in three directions: incorporating the wide-angle effect by adopting a local LOS definition for each galaxy in the 4PCF, accounting for tidal bias in the galaxy population, and generalising the assessment to an arbitrary cosmological background. Expanding the 4PCF in spherical harmonics, we show that angular momentum selection rules, encoded in the Wigner 3-j symbols, enforce that only parity-even contributions survive the integration over all LOS orientations, both in the plane-parallel approximation and in the full wide-angle case. This result is crucial for large-scale statistical analyses using isotropic estimators. It supports interpreting possible PV detections as a signal not due to a systematic RSD artefact. We conclude with a discussion of the caveats of our results and identify potential sources of PV.
papers.comment: 63 pages, 1 table, 5 figures. Ready for submission to Journal of Cosmology and Astroparticle Physics (JCAP)

papers.title: Can Mechanistic Interpretability Help Explain LLM Agent Failures? A Case Study on Web Element Hallucination
papers.summary: Mechanistic Interpretability (MI) has made significant progress in explaining the internal computations of Large Language Models (LLMs); however, these advances have yet to demonstrate comparable success in explaining the decision-making processes of LLM-based agents. This paper examines the challenges MI tools face when applied to realistic agentic failures. We focus on one such failure: web agents hallucinating actions that are not available on a website. We apply a series of mechanistic analyzes to Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct as it interacts with live websites. We find that a linear probe trained on the last prompt token can predict hallucinations before generation begins (0.80 AUC) and steering along a probe direction corrects 85\% of hallucinations, but disrupts 7\% of valid actions. However, these results only provide a partial explanation of why the agent hallucinates. The probe direction is sensitive to prompt formatting, losing much of its steering effect after a minor change to how actions are represented. Additionally, circuit identification can be difficult as the computation is distributed across multiple components and positions, and the information the agent relies on varies across examples. We discuss how these observations challenge the assumptions underlying standard MI methods for circuit discovery and feature identification, and outline future directions for making these methods better suited to explain failures in LLM-based agents.

papers.title: MeReader: An Offline, Privacy-Preserving, Progress-Aware AI Assistant for Narrative eBook Reading
papers.summary: This paper introduces MeReader, a privacy-preserving, offline and progress-aware AI assistant designed to function as a contextual companion for narrative reading on consumer hardware. Unlike conventional Large Language Model (LLM)-based systems that process documents/books online in an all-texts-at-once type of way, thereby risking narrative spoilers, MeReader confines both retrieval and generation to the reader's distinct position in the text. The system integrates a hybrid retrieval architecture, combining vector similarity, BM25, and summary embeddings, to ensure high fidelity to the reader's current context. We evaluate the system across classical English books using both quantitative comprehension metrics and qualitative LLM-based independent judging. The results identify a quality-latency frontier, showing that mid-sized local models (2b-4b) can achieve comprehension parity with larger counterparts (5b+) while maintaining acceptable response quality. Importantly, the proposed progress-aware boundary mechanism is shown to prevent future content leakage without compromising retrieval quality and correctness. These findings suggest that a localized, privacy-centric approach can augment, rather than replace, the digital reading experience, offering a good alternative to cloud-dependent services. Therein, there remains a lack of amalgamate systems which combine progress-aware, privacy-preserving, and narrative eBook reading with AI support. It is in this very gap that the development of MeReader came to be; synthesizing said strands into an offline, book-constrained assistant focused on enhancing comprehension without compromising narrative continuity or user privacy.

papers.title: Probing baryonic feedback using fast radio bursts and galaxy surveys
papers.summary: The dispersion measure (DM) of fast radio bursts (FRB) provides a noisy measure of the free-electron column density to the burst. With next-generation FRB surveys the number of bursts will drastically increase and measurements of the baryon distribution will be possible on the Mpc scales most relevant to Stage IV weak lensing surveys. Comparing the DM auto-spectrum, DM-shear cross-spectrum and the kinetic Sunyaev-Zel'dovich effect, we argue that the cross-correlation of FRB catalogs with galaxy surveys offers many advantages. Hybrid Effective Field Theory (HEFT), often used in large-scale structure cosmology, is capable of modeling the clustering of electrons jointly with galaxies and matter to small scales. Using HEFT with the Padé model of baryonic feedback, we forecast that next-generation FRB surveys (combined with galaxy samples) will be able to constrain feedback at a level informative for Stage IV weak lensing surveys. In particular we should not be limited by modeling the manner in which galaxies trace the matter field. Rather constraints of the higher-order electron biases and the electron-galaxy cross-stochasticity provide the dominant limitation, and are an obvious target for improvement in order to reach percent-level constraints. The same measurements also provide a valuable means of constraining feedback in hydrodynamic simulations of galaxy formation in a way that is not tied to the modeling of particular galaxy samples.

papers.title: On numerical issues of divergences between nearly equal distributions
papers.summary: Barron et al. (2026) recently identified numerical issues in the softmax and soft cross-entropy loss. We show that similar issues are present in standard divergence operations between categorical distributions. This includes the forward and reverse Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence and generalized Jensen-Shannon divergence (JSD), as well as Monte Carlo KL estimates and entropy. When the distributions are nearly equal, rounding and cancellation issues affect the forward and gradient computations. These issues can affect settings using divergences in optimization objectives, such as knowledge distillation, reinforcement learning, and proximal methods. We propose numerically stable reformulations and provide example implementations for each setting, validated by property-based tests.

papers.title: Complex fluid flow dynamics by bright scattershot boson sampling
papers.summary: Boson sampling machines have become a fruitful tool for establishing new concepts, which connect fundamental physics with computer science applications. Here, we exploit the intrinsically high-dimensional correlations generated by the measurement outcomes of a multiphoton boson sampling machine and demonstrate how a reconfigurable architecture can be programmed to autonomously model the time evolution of nonlinear dynamical systems that describe complex fluid flows. By extending on the original scattershot boson sampling (SBS) scheme to include higher photon number components -- a scheme which we label bright scattershot boson sampling (BSBS) --- this scheme overcomes scaling issues inherent to SBS-based schemes by utilizing all randomly generated input photon number distributions. We illustrate the capability of this scheme for two complex fluid-flow models: an eight-dimensional Lorenz-type model of two-dimensional thermally driven convection and a 16-dimensional model of global atmospheric circulation. Using a digital twin of the BSBS architecture based on multiphoton statistics, we show that the photonic approach accurately reproduces the temporal dynamics of both systems while being resilient to photon losses of up to 50 per cent. We also verified that the BSBS case outperforms a comparable run with coherent light. Moreover, its prediction horizon exceeds that of a classical reservoir-computing model with the same query complexity. These results highlight the potential of near-term photonic quantum computing for addressing relevant real-world tasks on noisy intermediate-scale devices.

papers.title: An All-Digital Coherent AFSK Demodulator for CubeSat Applications
papers.summary: Audio frequency-shift keying (AFSK) is a widely adopted modulation scheme for CubeSat systems due to its favorable bandwidth efficiency and implementation simplicity. However, coherent detection usually is avoided because synchronization impairments, caused by intense line-of-sight (LOS) dynamics inherent in low Earth orbit (LEO), may significantly degrade the bit error rate (BER). This paper presents a new all-digital coherent AFSK demodulator based on a Kalman filter (KF) for carrier phase and timing delay synchronization and the Viterbi algorithm for bit detection. The Viterbi algorithm is employed for maximum likelihood sequence detection, and the detected bit statistics are fed back to the KF to estimate phase shift, Doppler frequency shift, and Doppler drift induced by the LOS dynamics. Original mathematical analyses are derived to provide a theoretical foundation for the proposed demodulator's operation, specifically addressing its synchronization accuracy in dynamic LEO environments. The proposed demodulator is evaluated considering an additive white Gaussian noise channel with real CubeSat orbits. The performance results obtained through computer simulations demonstrate that the proposed model can withstand such scenarios with a gain of 5 dB in terms of BER compared to the conventional noncoherent AFSK demodulator. The KF performance is assessed using a moving root-mean-square error (MRMSE) statistic and the trace of its state error covariance matrix estimate.

papers.title: Restoring Consistency with Poynting's Theorem in Numerical MHD and RMHD
papers.summary: For perfectly conducting plasmas, Poynting's theorem states that the time rate of change of electromagnetic energy density equals the negative of the divergence of the Poynting flux. To the best of our knowledge, this involutive theorem has never been mimetically incorporated in codes. We show that there is an inconsistency in MHD and RMHD codes that evolve face-centered magnetic fields in globally-divergence-free fashion. This is because the face-centered flux of energy density, which incorporates a Poynting vector, is evaluated using one-dimensional Riemann solvers that are applied at face-centers. However, the face-centered magnetic fields are evolved according to edge-centered electric fields that come from two-dimensional Riemann solvers that are applied to the edges of a zone. While edge-centered electric fields are used to evolve the magnetic field, they have no influence on the face-centered Poynting flux. For situations where the magnetic energy is much larger than the thermal energy, this causes a negative pressure to be evaluated at the zone-centers. This paper restores consistency by using edge-centered variables to evaluate a face-centered Poynting flux. A simple accuracy-preserving correction is made to the face-centered flux of energy density. We show that it helps considerably in simulations that have very strong magnetic fields.

papers.title: Asymptotic Margins and Feature Confinement in Conic Classification Heads under Softmax Cross-Entropy
papers.summary: Classification heads built on conic functions give each class a bounded region of the feature space, and such regions are used to reject samples of unseen classes. We ask whether these regions also keep the features bounded when the head is trained with softmax cross-entropy. For a head whose class scores combine a linear term with a Euclidean norm, we first show that the region of each class is bounded by a quadric of revolution, whose eccentricity is the reciprocal of one learned ratio. We then attach to each class an asymptotic margin, which compares the growth of its score with the growth of all the other scores and can be computed by a second-order cone program. The loss of a class has infimum zero exactly when its margin is positive, and it then approaches zero only along diverging features. When the margin is negative, the loss is coercive and its minimizers lie in an explicit ball. Since softmax depends only on the differences between scores, a class with a bounded region can still have a positive margin, so bounded regions do not confine the features. The result extends to other norms, including the polyhedral conic functions. On CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, all 1210 cells of 67 trained conic heads have positive margins, whereas a prototype head keeps nine of its ten cells bounded, as the theory predicts.
papers.comment: 22 pages, 2 figures. Companion paper: to be uploaded. Code: https://github.com/ongerek/Conic

papers.title: Agentic induction of common data elements and information extraction from sarcoma case report abstracts
papers.summary: Common data elements (CDEs) support clinical data comparability but are usually defined manually. We investigated whether large language model agents could derive a CDE schema from sarcoma case report abstracts and apply it at scale. An agent proposed 72,909 candidate CDEs from 24,588 PubMed abstracts; agentic consolidation yielded 1,570 CDEs. We retained 53 supported by at least 50 abstracts and attempted evidence-linked extraction across the corpus. Processing succeeded for all retained CDEs in 79.2% of abstracts, including responses indicating non-mention. Two human reviewers approved 83.0% of retained CDEs for relevance, 67.9% for clarity, and 56.6% for correctness. In 100 sampled abstracts, exact agreement with the value extracted by the LLM was 94.9% among 1,116 pairs with a non-empty answer (abstract-level bootstrap 95% CI, 93.0-96.4%). Errors concentrated in anatomical and temporal fields. These findings support agent-assisted schema drafting followed by expert curation before large-scale extraction.

papers.title: Disturbance-Aware Informative Planning in Spatiotemporal Environments
papers.summary: Autonomous robots are widely used for persistent monitoring of spatiotemporal environments, where quantities of interest (QoI) change across space and time and require repeated measurements. In practice, robot motion can be affected by external disturbances that vary across the environment. When such external disturbances are not considered in trajectory optimization, it can lead to inaccurate predictions of robot motion and, consequently, the information acquired about the QoI during execution. However, estimating disturbances throughout the environment can be inefficient, as disturbances in regions with little overlap with monitoring trajectories have limited impact on monitoring performance. We therefore propose a two-stage informative planning framework for unknown, spatially varying but time-invariant disturbances, combining informed disturbance sampling with disturbance-aware trajectory optimization. First, we identify where QoI measurements are needed and generate alternative paths to these locations using the environment geometry. We then prioritize disturbance measurements based on their expected reduction of disturbance uncertainty along these paths. Second, rather than optimizing information acquisition based on nominal robot motion, we incorporate the learned disturbance belief into trajectory optimization to account for its effects on robot motion and information acquisition. Across four simulation scenarios, the proposed method reduces disturbance-learning time by 25.0--52.3 percent compared with environment-wide estimation and identifies paths that appear costly under nominal dynamics but become preferable when disturbances are considered.
papers.comment: Submitted to Learning for Dynamics and Control Conference 2027. Project website: https://kalebbennaveed.github.io/dist-aware-ipp/

papers.title: Agentic AI for Discovering Fault-Tolerant Quantum Circuits
